sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Ownership and Cross-Border Sub-Licensing of Trademarks and Patents

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: English Common Law statutory foundation with limited customary (fa'amatai) law elements; company, commercial, and trust law governed by statutes and common law doctrines
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa–China Framework Agreement on Comprehensive Economic Cooperation (signed 2011)
Samoa–China Agreement on Trade in Goods (effective 2015)
Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER-Plus), signed 14 June 2017
OECD Global Forum-aligned Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) and Exchange of Information on Request (EOIR) arrangements with Australia, New Zealand and other G20 partners
Limited full double-tax treaty network; no comprehensive DTA with the People's Republic of China as of assessment date

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended 1998, 2008, 2013) ss. 5, 6, 9, 10; International Companies (Amendment) Act 2018 (beneficial ownership record-keeping obligations); Companies Act 2001 as amended by Companies (Amendment) Act 2018, Part XI-A (Register of Beneficial Owners, applied by analogy and supervisory extension to International Companies); Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2000; Money Laundering Prevention Regulations 2008 (as amended) and AML/CFT Directive 2018; Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2002

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of each beneficial owner's national passport (bio-data page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the beneficial owner's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa a Contracting Party since 13 March 2019; China-sourced notarial copies apostilled via Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank of the beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where notarized, or banker's certification if issued directly by a financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / certificate of good standing of any corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank of the corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if issued in an HCCH Contracting Party; otherwise consular legalization at the Samoan Consulate/Embassy or designated diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney appointing the SIFA-licensed registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Beneficial owner or authorized corporate officer of the applicant entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization + Hague Apostille (or consular legalization where the execution country is not an HCCH Contracting Party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form and source-of-wealth statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Beneficial owner executing before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization; original transmitted to Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) via the registered agent; no public filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory initial and continuous screening of every director, shareholder (at or above 25%), and authorized signatory against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) OFAC SDN List; (iii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iv) Samoa national sanctions list administered by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and the Financial Intelligence Unit; and (v) adverse-media and enforcement databases. Politically Exposed Persons (domestic and foreign) are identified under s. 2 Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and are subject to enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, and verified source-of-wealth documentation. Screening is executed by the SIFA-licensed registered agent, recorded in the client's AML file, and re-run no less than quarterly and upon any trigger event; high-risk jurisdiction relationships require additional verification and may be declined at the agent's discretion.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – International Companies Registry (electronic filing exclusively through SIFA-licensed registered agents; public gateway: sifa.ws)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary registered name must be in Latin script and end with a permitted suffix ('Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Société Anonyme' or abbreviations 'Ltd', 'Corp', 'Inc', 'SA'). A parallel non-Latin script name, including Chinese, is permissible upon SIFA approval as a transliterated or translated secondary name; the Latin-script name must be unique and not confusingly similar to any existing or reserved name on the Samoa registries, and the non-Latin name must not contravene public policy or misrepresent the entity's licensed status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with SIFA within 14 calendar days, specifying grounds of distinctiveness, bona fide intention to use, and rebutting the Registrar's stated objections; the appeal may request a further 30-day reservation extension if the rejection is cured by a minor amendment. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may file a fresh name application with a modified name and a new fee. SIFA's final decision is subject to judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Ordinance 1961.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Samoa International Company must at all times maintain a registered office in Samoa at the premises of its licensed registered agent (International Companies Act 1987 s. 9). The Company itself is not required to maintain physical business premises in Samoa; a purely virtual and remote operational structure for a global IP HoldCo is lawful, provided the registered agent's physical address serves as the statutory service-of-process and venue address. Virtual-office arrangements supplied by third parties outside the registered agent's premises do not satisfy the statutory requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for the International Company's own premises (estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection of own premises: 5–10%); the licensed registered agent's office is subject to routine SIFA and AML/CFT supervisory on-site inspections approximately every 12–24 months, with possible targeted document inspection and verification of client files. A tax-exempt IC without domestic trading activity carries a de-minimis risk of operational interruption.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 5-12 (Incorporation), s. 7 (Registered Office), s. 56 (Directors and Officers)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form IC-1, Application for Incorporation of an International Company
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required. Issued capital may be partly paid; no escrow deposit is mandated under the International Companies Act 1987.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the subscribers to the Memorandum and Articles of Association be and are hereby confirmed as shareholders of Samoa International Company; (2) That the registered office of the Company be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Samoa, and the agent be and is authorized to file all statutory notices; (3) That the persons named in the consent forms are appointed directors and secretary, each to serve until the next annual general meeting; (4) That the directors are authorized to allot fully paid shares, open bank accounts, execute royalty agreements, and engage professional advisers; (5) That this resolution shall take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Name Registry via a licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company name to SIFA through the licensed registered agent for availability and permissibility review under s. 10 of the International Companies Act 1987. Concurrently execute a registered agent engagement letter and complete the required customer due diligence information.
required_dossiers: Duly signed registered agent engagement letter
Proposed corporate name and up to two alternative names
Identification documents, proof of address, and beneficial ownership information for all proposed shareholders and officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as unavailable or objectionable, the registered agent files a fresh name application with alternative names within 2 business days; no additional government fee is charged for resubmission within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in a form permitted under the International Companies Act 1987. The incorporator and initial subscriber execute the application before a notary or a witness recognized in a Common Law jurisdiction, and the registered agent submits Form IC-1, the constitution, declarations, and supporting consents to SIFA.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association signed by the subscriber and notarized as appropriate
Consent of each named director and the secretary
Registered agent certificate of acceptance and registered office address in Samoa
Declaration as to the intended lawful activity and absence of any local conducting of business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA issues a query, the registered agent must file a formal response and any corrected instrument within 14 calendar days; a simple correction endorsement will issue without a new inspection unless the proposed change affects the fundamental structure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration, Stamp Duty, and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon SIFA approval of the incorporation instrument, pay the statutory registration fee and stamp duty by wire transfer to the official SIFA bank account. The Registrar will then register the company in the International Companies Register and issue the Certificate of Incorporation to the registered agent.
required_dossiers: SIFA approval or conditional approval notice
Proof of payment of registration fee and stamp duty
Registered agent signed receipt for the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misapplied or delayed, the registered agent submits the bank remittance reference to SIFA and, where necessary, requests a receipt correction. Overpayments are refunded after written application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) / Licensed Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pass the pro-forma first board resolution to adopt the registered office, appoint the initial directors and secretary, approve the issue of shares, and authorize the opening of bank or payment system accounts. Maintain the statutory registers and corporate records at the registered agent's office and file any annual return or declaration required under the International Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Consent and appointment forms for directors and secretary
Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
Registered agent confirmation of registered office and records inspection
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SIFA queries beneficial ownership or record-keeping matters, the agent must file corrected schedules or declarations within 10 business days. Minor inadvertent late filings may be cured by payment of the applicable late fee and written explanation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable -- no industrial licensing board requirement for a non-resident IP holding company under ISIC 6420 in Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable -- the International Company holds no physical establishment and is exempt from local business licensing on cross-border IP royalty activities

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa -- Environmental Impact Assessment Division (where relevant)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt -- pure IP patent and trademark licensing with no physical project, no construction, and no installation of equipment in Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. No wastewater, air emissions, volatile organic compounds, hazardous waste, or thermal discharge streams arise from the licensing activity. There is no environmental compliance obligation under Samoa law for this non-physical scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable -- no employees, premises, or industrial operations in Samoa. The registered office is situated at the licensed agent's address, and the agent maintains compliance with all relevant administrative and safety certifications. Fire safety and structural load approvals are not triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Samoa Ministry for Revenue (Tax and Customs Administration), official portal: www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity incorporated as an International Company under the International Companies Act 2016 must submit Form R1 (Taxpayer Registration) to the Samoa Ministry for Revenue, accompanied by the certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, director/shareholder passport copies, and registered office details. The Ministry issues a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) within 5 business days. For entities relying exclusively on international company tax exemption, a Certificate of Exempt Status may also be obtained.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: International Company tax-exempt status applies automatically by statute; no check-the-box election exists. An International Company that carries on business within Samoa may, under the Income Tax Act 2015, be treated as a taxable resident entity for Samoa-source income only. No hybrid mismatch elections are available under Samoa law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual value of taxable supplies; non-resident suppliers of offshore services must register regardless of local threshold if Samoa source taxation applies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory electronic invoicing clearance or digital API stamping regime exists in Samoa. Registered suppliers must issue a standard tax invoice containing prescribed particulars (name, TIN, description, amount, VAGST charged) within 28 days of supply.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated when exported from Samoa within 28 days of supply and supporting documentary evidence is retained. Services are zero-rated when supplied to a non-resident, the direct benefit occurs outside Samoa, and the recipient is not a Samoa resident. Royalties or license fees from foreign patents and trademarks payable to an International Company are, by reason of the company's offshore tax-exempt status, outside the VAGST net; where VAGST-registered, such supplies will be zero-rated on proof of foreign receipt.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsupported export zero-rating claims attract a shortfall penalty of up to 200% of the tax evaded, monthly interest of 1.5%, and restoration of any refund received. Criminal sanctions include fines up to WST 20,000 per offence and imprisonment up to 3 years under the Tax Administration Act 2012 and the Customs Act 2014.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) (Samoan: Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa), exercising statutory powers under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 (as amended), the Financial Institutions Act 1996, the Exchange Control Act 1976 and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended). The CBS is the sole foreign-exchange control authority, licensed-bank supervisor and operator of the national payment and clearing infrastructure; offshore vehicle supervision is delegated in part to the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), and AML reporting is received by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is fully convertible for current-account transactions (royalties, trade, services, dividends) and partially convertible for capital-account transactions, which require case-by-case CBS approval for residents. The WS_IC, as a non-resident International Company, is statutorily outside the Exchange Control Act 1976 and may therefore receive, hold and disburse USD, EUR and AUD without prior CBS approval; no mandatory conversion into WST applies to its offshore royalty receipts. Practical hurdles: (i) the WST has no deliverable offshore market and is managed against a trade-weighted basket, so all material treasury flows should be denominated in USD; (ii) any conversion of foreign currency into WST for local agent fees must be executed through a licensed authorised dealer and is subject to CBS large-transaction reporting; (iii) foreign-parent profit repatriation through the IC is lawful without CBS pre-approval, but upstream distributions must be documented as dividends under the IC constitution to prevent recharacterisation as a taxable royalty by the destination jurisdiction; and (iv) the IC's tax-exempt status requires a contemporaneous economic-substance file to avoid regulatory classification as an abusive shell or brass-plate vehicle.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Act 1976 and CBS implementing notices, resident exporters of goods and services (including royalty income treated as invisible exports) must: (1) collect export proceeds within 180 days of the date of exportation or invoicing; (2) route all receipts through an authorised dealer in Samoa; and (3) offer the foreign-currency proceeds for conversion into WST within 30 days of crediting, unless an approved foreign-currency account or a CBS deferral is in force. The WS_IC, being a non-resident International Company, is exempt from these surrender obligations under the International Companies Act 1987, provided that all royalty income remains in foreign-currency accounts and no WST conversion occurs for the benefit of a Samoan resident without passing through an authorised dealer. Resident sub-licensees owing royalties to the IC must nevertheless satisfy the 180-day collection and 30-day offer-for-sale rules in their own export documentation, and the IC should require contractual confirmation of this compliance from each resident counterparty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Treasury Account - Offshore Foreign Currency Account (USD/EUR/AUD) with full SWIFT direct clearing; the preferred clearing gateway for non-resident International Companies.
Operational Foreign Currency Account (USD/AUD) plus WST Domestic Settlement Account; accepts International Companies but applies stricter substance documentation.
Domestic WST Operational Account only; limited appetite and clearing capability for non-resident offshore IP-holding structures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-Low. Samoa has no licensing framework for independent EMI or e-money providers; the Financial Institutions Act 1996 confines deposit-taking and payment services to licensed commercial banks, and the CBS does not recognise offshore EMI licences as authorised-dealer status. A non-resident International Company may lawfully operate an offshore EMI account (for example Airwallex, Wise Business or Currenxie) as a collections aggregator for USD/EUR royalty receipts, provided the EMI is appropriately licensed in its home jurisdiction and the IC's Samoan registered agent is notified. Legal constraints: (i) the EMI must not become the place of effective management of the IC, or SIFA may challenge the Samoan tax-exempt and substance status; (ii) an offshore EMI cannot clear WST, obtain CBS approvals or settle domestic Samoan payments; (iii) correspondent banks frequently restrict IP-heavy and royalty-heavy flows to EMIs; and (iv) the Samoan AML framework treats the offshore EMI as an additional relationship requiring enhanced due diligence and annual declaration. Recommended structure: maintain the ANZ or BSP account as the principal clearing and treasury gateway, and use the EMI solely for low-value collection aggregation with a daily sweep back to the Samoan bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not expressly mandated by CBS statute, but in practice all three licensed banks require at least one director, the ultimate beneficial owner, or a duly authorised signatory to attend a face-to-face account-opening interview at a Samoan branch before a first-time non-resident International Company can activate an account. Fully remote account opening is not publicly offered. Where the principal cannot travel, the IC may appoint a Samoan-licensed management company or a director to attend under a notarised Power of Attorney, presenting original board resolutions, certified passports, corporate registers and a bank reference for each ultimate beneficial owner. ANZ will occasionally waive the physical interview for an established international law-firm introducer following a video KYC call and enhanced due diligence; BSP and Samoa Commercial Bank generally insist on a physical meeting. Passport copies must be notarised or certified by the registered agent, and all non-resident directors must complete source-of-wealth declarations; biometric or video verification alone is not accepted without a reputable introducer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: non-resident IP holding company with no employees, no rented office and no board activity in Samoa, assessed as a brass-plate or shell-company risk by the onboarding bank.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SIFA economic-substance compliance file comprising: (i) current certificate from the licensed Samoan registered agent confirming a physical registered office under a service agreement; (ii) board minutes for each financial year evidencing meetings held in Samoa or by video as permitted by the constitution, with strategic IP management decisions recorded; (iii) a core-income-generating-activity (CIGA) narrative demonstrating that licensing negotiation, contract management, IP oversight and royalty administration are performed in Samoa or by the Samoan agent under an intra-group services agreement; (iv) OECD modified-nexus calculations evidencing qualifying expenditures meeting the substance threshold applicable to IP entities (or the reduced threshold for a pure equity holding company, as applicable); and (v) a signed declaration that the IC holds a valid SIFA economic-substance certificate for the relevant accounting period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: ultimate beneficial owners or the parent entity resident in a jurisdiction on the EU List of Non-Cooperative Jurisdictions, the FATF grey list, or a high-risk third country for AML purposes, triggering enhanced due diligence and potential refusal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence pack including: audited consolidated financial statements of the parent entity; certificate of tax residence of the parent from its revenue authority; individual source-of-wealth statements for each ultimate beneficial owner; bank reference letters issued by the parent's regulated bank within the preceding three months; certified copies of passports and proof of address; the executed master licence agreement evidencing genuine commercial purpose; evidence of an active tax information exchange relationship between Samoa and the parent's jurisdiction; and a client-acceptance memorandum from a Samoan law firm accepting AML oversight responsibility for the relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: large recurring royalty flows from or to tax-exempt jurisdictions, interpreted by the bank as potential transfer mispricing, base erosion, or abusive tax structuring involving hard-to-value intangibles.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full transfer-pricing and valuation dossier: an OECD-compliant transfer-pricing report benchmarking the royalty rate against comparable trademark and patent licensing transactions; an independent IP valuation report using the income or relief-from-royalty method; executed licence and sub-licence agreements with clear commercial terms and exclusivity provisions; a country-by-country description of CIGA performed in Samoa evidencing alignment of value creation with the Samoan entity; a Samoan tax-clearance certificate confirming no outstanding domestic tax liability; and, where treaty relief or limitation-of-benefits protection is relied upon, a supporting legal opinion from a recognised international tax counsel.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: sudden high-value inbound capital injection for the acquisition of intellectual property from a parent, exceeding the CBS large-transaction reporting threshold of WST 100,000 equivalent, raising potential money-laundering or source-of-funds concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transactional dossier assembled for the bank and the FIU: board resolution authorising the capital contribution and IP acquisition; updated share register evidencing the allotment of shares or advancement of shareholder loan; the executed sale-and-contribution agreement for the IP assets; an independent valuation supporting the consideration; the inbound SWIFT MT103 instruction with Field 70 narrative 'Equity injection for acquisition of IP assets under Board Resolution dated [date]' issued by the contributing entity's bank; source-of-funds confirmation from the paying bank; a certificate of incumbency from the Samoan registered agent; and current beneficial-ownership registers under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: the parent (for example a Hong Kong or Singapore holding company) instructs its bank to issue a SWIFT MT103 credit to the WS_IC account at ANZ Bank (Samoa) Limited or BSP Samoa. The wire must carry: Field 50K (ordering customer: parent entity), Field 57A (beneficiary bank and SWIFT address), Field 59 (beneficiary: WS_IC, exact account number), Field 70 (remittance information stating the precise purpose, e.g. 'Equity contribution for IP acquisition pursuant to Board Resolution dated [date]' or 'Shareholder loan disbursement under Loan Agreement dated [date]'), and Field 71A (charges: SHA). No CBS prior approval is required because the International Company exemption under the International Companies Act 1987 removes the Exchange Control Act 1976 reporting and surrender obligations for foreign-currency credits to a non-resident entity. The receiving bank nonetheless verifies the certificate of incorporation, SIFA economic-substance certificate, board resolution, contributor identity and source of funds; credits in excess of WST 100,000 equivalent are reported to the Samoa FIU as large-transaction reports. If the IC later converts part of the injection into WST for local cost payments, the conversion must be executed through an authorised dealer and may require a CBS application supported by the Samoan agent's invoices.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 international wire for outbound royalty disbursements to non-resident licensors, patent owners, sub-agents and intra-group service providers; each instruction must reference the underlying licence agreement, the commercial invoice and, for related-party payees, a board resolution approving the payment. The IC, as a tax-exempt non-resident entity, is not obliged to deduct Samoan withholding tax on royalties paid to non-residents, but must obtain a Samoan tax-clearance certificate if the payee is a Samoan tax resident; (2) Commercial documentary letters of credit issued or confirmed through ANZ or BSP under UCP600 for security-backed IP acquisitions or purchases of tangible collateral, with the traditional transport documents replaced by IP assignment certificates, notarised licence agreements and insurance certificates where no physical goods are shipped; (3) Same-day real-time gross settlement is not available for cross-border WST, so all settlements clear through the USD correspondent banking network. For related-party payouts exceeding USD 500,000 equivalent, the IC should pre-position with the bank a SIFA or registered-agent countersigned direction letter, an updated economic-substance calculation and the executed disbursement schedule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forwards: outright deliverable forward contracts with a Samoan authorised dealer (ANZ or BSP Treasury) on USD, EUR, AUD or NZD against WST for documented commercial receipts or payments; CBS administrative practice permits corporate hedges up to a maximum tenor of 12 months, subject to production of the underlying royalty or licence agreement evidencing genuine exposure.

NDFs: non-deliverable forwards on WST executed with international bank desks in Singapore or Hong Kong, used because no deliverable offshore WST market exists; permissible without CBS approval for a non-resident International Company as the Exchange Control Act 1976 does not apply to the IC's foreign-currency transactions, but the hedge must be documented under an ISDA confirmation and supported by a commercial purpose statement.

Currency swaps: cross-currency swaps (USD/EUR against WST or USD against EUR) executed under an ISDA Master Agreement with a top-tier offshore counterparty or via ANZ/BSP Treasury; no regulatory approval is required for a non-resident IC, but the bank and counterparty must be satisfied that the swap serves a genuine commercial purpose, such as servicing IP-acquisition debt, and is not a speculative or unhedged derivative position.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee (Annual Renewal of International Company Registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Financial Services Authority (SIFSA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each anniversary of incorporation; payment due on or before the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of 10% of the annual fee per month or part of a month; unpaid annual fees for three consecutive months may trigger administrative strike-off under the International Companies Act 1987.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registered Office and Licensed Registered Agent (lodged through the resident agent as part of the renewal package)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Licensed Registered Agent maintaining the registered office in Apia; records kept on file for SIFSA inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of incorporation together with the annual government fee payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a licensed resident agent or a registered office in Samoa is a continuing statutory default and may result in the Registrar striking the company off; the agent may resign without cause, precipitating administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and Shareholder/Director Ledger Confirmation (conducted by the licensed registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered agent at the registered office; internal compliance record, no public lodging with SIFSA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At each anniversary of incorporation, concurrently with the annual renewal package; any share transfer occurring during the preceding year must be reflected in the register before sign-off
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Deficiencies in the statutory registers may be reported to SIFSA by the agent under AML/CFT obligations; persistent failure to maintain the registers may support enforcement action under the International Companies Act 1987 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2007.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None. Samoa International Companies are unconditionally exempt from statutory audit under the International Companies Act 1987 unless the company's articles of association expressly require an audit or the Registrar directs an examination. Revenue, asset, and headcount thresholds are therefore not applicable to the standard IP licensing HoldCo.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No specific statutory accounting standard is prescribed for International Companies; books of account must be kept as sufficient to disclose the true financial position of the company with reasonable accuracy, and may be prepared on an IFRS or simplified accrual basis. Where consolidated group reporting is required by a foreign parent, IFRS is the customary convention.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Samoa does not maintain a public beneficial ownership register for International Companies. The licensed registered agent holds a confidential ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) file separate from the statutory registers. No standalone UBO annual confirmation filing is required by statute, but the agent must update the internal UBO record upon any share transfer and the register of members must be endorsed with the transfer. The agent performs an annual portfolio review and confirmation to the company under its AML/CFT obligations pursuant to the Financial Services Authority Act 2010 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2007.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges (where any charge exists)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,000–US$2,500 per annum (licensed registered agent and registered office package, excluding government fee and disbursements)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000–US$15,000 per annum for a certified audit of an IP licensing HoldCo if adopted voluntarily or mandated by a parent group; audit is not legally mandatory for a standard Samoa International Company

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies (ICs) are fully exempt from Samoan corporate income tax on all worldwide income, including IP royalties, capital gains, and dividend income, pursuant to the International Companies Act 1987. The exemption operates as a statutory tax holiday in perpetuity. No payroll tax, social security contribution, or branch profits tax applies to a non-resident owned IC. The only recurring government levy is an annual license fee of WST 1,000 paid to the Samoa International Companies Registry.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is required for an exempt International Company. The mandatory filing is the International Company Annual Return (Form IC-AR), submitted electronically to the Samoa International Companies Registry through a licensed registered agent's secure portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Return is due within three months after the anniversary of incorporation, as prescribed in the International Companies Act. A non-resident IC may file earlier if the registered agent obtains the relevant consent; no CIT filing applies because the entity is outside the income tax net.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name shown on the Certificate of Incorporation, including the suffix International Company or IC.
Provide a physical street address maintained by the registered agent; a post office box is not sufficient.
List all directors with full legal names and residential addresses; corporate directors are permitted but must appoint an individual representative.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Shareholder register and beneficial ownership declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) on the confidential register; non-resident shareholders need not be Samoan residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of tax-exempt status and economic substance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the company claims exemption as an IC and state the location of core IP management activities; if none exist in Samoa, describe offshore substance arrangements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the Annual Return attracts a fixed penalty of WST 500 plus a daily surcharge of WST 50 per day, capped at 90 days. Failure to file for six consecutive months triggers automatic strike-off from the Registry, with a reinstatement fee of WST 750 and potential personal liability for directors for outstanding fees and penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (dividends paid by a tax-exempt International Company to non-resident shareholders are not subject to Samoan withholding tax)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the IC is exempt, no Samoan withholding tax arises on distributions. Where a double taxation agreement (e.g., Samoa–China DTA) is voluntarily invoked, the non-resident payee must submit a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its home jurisdiction, together with Samoa Revenue Form WHT-T, before the payment date. Revenue grants the relief in writing; retroactive refunds require a formal assessment objection within 30 days of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 15% for royalties and 15% for interest derived from a Samoa source. Treaty rates under applicable DTAs are typically 10% for royalties and interest, subject to beneficial ownership and limitation-on-benefits clauses. In practice, an IC receiving licensing income from a non-resident licensee will not suffer Samoa WHT; payments made by an IC to a foreign licensor outside Samoa are not sourced in Samoa and therefore escape WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Samoan entity must prepare a Local File and Master File if its aggregate related-party transactions exceed WST 15 million per annum, or if the group's consolidated revenue exceeds WST 100 million. For an exempt IC, the Revenue may still demand contemporaneous documentation where the licensing margin appears inconsistent with arm's length returns.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Samoa International Companies (Economic Substance) Act applies to IP holding companies. Such an IC must demonstrate that core income-generating activities are managed and directed in Samoa, including regular board meetings, availability of qualified employees, physical premises, and operational expenditure proportionate to IP income. Outsourcing to a Samoan licensed service provider is acceptable, but the annual substance return must be filed with the Registry. Non-compliance results in penalties, exchange of information with foreign tax authorities, and potential strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent IP Licensing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating royalty income, fabricating sub-license agreements, creating backdated assignments, or sending false financial statements to the Samoa Revenue Authority to preserve tax-exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction attracts a fine not exceeding WST 1,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 7 years. Civil assessment may impose 200% of the tax underpaid (if any), with interest compounded at 20% per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where a director signs or directs a false filing; directors are jointly and severally liable for restitution of hidden licensing fees, personal travel bans can be issued pending investigation, and imprisonment applies upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the patent licensing vehicle without physical presence in Samoa, no substantive board meetings, no accounting records, and pure pass-through royalties without local decision-making.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A penalty equal to 10% of the IP-derived income for each non-compliant year, capped at WST 2,000,000, plus potential de-registration and adverse exchange of information to the beneficial owner's tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the annual substance penalty if they were aware of the sham structure; the Court may impose director disqualification for up to 10 years, freeze personal assets, and order restitution of fees earned from the arrangement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain an accurate beneficial ownership register, failing to perform KYC on ultimate owners, or allowing the IC to be a conduit for untraceable wire transfers tied to royalty payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to WST 50,000 per offence per director; the registered agent's license may be suspended; the IC may be subject to regulatory audit and compulsory liquidation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face up to 3 years imprisonment for money laundering facilitation, personal fines up to WST 100,000, and civil asset forfeiture of funds passing through the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising an excessive dividend as a royalty, management fee, or interest payment to shift profits out of Samoa without commercial substance or to avoid contractual tax gross-ups.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Revenue recharacterizes the payment as a dividend, imposes a 15% dividend withholding tax (reduced to 0% for an exempt IC but exposed to treaty abuse), and applies a 20% negligence penalty plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the sham can be ordered to repay the distribution personally if the company is insolvent; travel bans, contempt proceedings, and criminal sanctions apply for failure to comply with the Revenue's demand.
